subject.title: Agent-created crons inherit session toolsAllow at create-time; patch toolsAllow:null is a silent no-op; claude-cli backend then refuses the job

question: How should OpenClaw handle agent-created CLI-backed cron jobs that inherit or retain `toolsAllow` without making explicit per-cron restrictions fail open?
rationale: The current source intentionally recaps restricted agent updates and intentionally fails closed when a CLI backend receives a runtime allow-list it cannot enforce, so choosing early rejection, narrow repair, or runtime relaxation changes a tool-policy security boundary.

options.title: Reject or Explain Restricted Clears
options.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary, return an explicit agent-facing error for blocked null clears, and add a narrow doctor/operator repair for provably auto-default stale caps.

options.title: Authorize Narrow Agent Clear
options.body: Allow only inherited default caps to be cleared through the agent cron tool while preserving explicit restrictions and proving the distinction with tests.

options.title: Relax CLI Runtime Handling
options.body: Warn and ignore selected inherited caps at runtime on CLI-backed jobs, accepting that those restrictions are not enforced by the backend.

recommendation.title: Reject or Explain Restricted Clears
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary, return an explicit agent-facing error for blocked null clears, and add a narrow doctor/operator repair for provably auto-default stale caps.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored the latest marker-preservation fix and is closest to the current service/edit semantics that decide whether the marker is preserved, cleared, or recapped.
